subject: Initial discovery + model-eval & safety brief for Everest Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom@everesthealth.ai>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina@everesthealth.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 14:32:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: discovery + recommended next steps (model fit & safety)

Tom / Lina — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. I included Dev and Evelyn on this thread so we can move from discovery into a short eval loop.

Call highlights (as I heard them):
- Primary use case: patient intake triage + FAQ routing across 3 specialties (~60k requests/month; 95th p90 latency target 400ms).
- Hard constraints: PHI in prompts, auditability, ability to refuse on certain clinical/legal questions, and clear guardrails for drug/dosage/referral guidance.
- Success metrics: <=5% critical safety failures on our eval set; generation latency <500ms p95; acceptable cost band for pilot.

Recommended model path for initial pilot:
1) Redwood-run gptq-health-6B (quantized 4-bit) — good balance of safety fine-tuning and latency.
2) Fallback: open-llm/fast-med-13B (higher quality but higher cost) only for long-context clinical summaries.

Attached: prompt sets you can review (Everest_promptsets_v1.json) and our benchmark snapshot (redwood_eval_benchmarks_ev_20260224.csv). I also linked our Hugging Face stub and a Drive folder with the full automated eval harness.

Safety / refusal behavior notes:
- We ran the standard Redwood safety suite plus a custom clinical refusal set you described. For gptq-health-6B it refused unsafe medication directives in 94% of the original prompt set; we saw a few soft-failures where the model responded with hedged clinical content instead of a firm refusal.
- Action recommended: add explicit refusal templates and a two-stage classifier fallback (fast intent classifier -> strict refusal template) for top-level triage prompts. Dev has a proposed classifier prompt in his note below.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) We’ll run a 1-week sandbox eval using your redacted production prompts and our prompt sets (you provide sample prompts; we can sanitize).
2) Dev will propose a classifier + guardrail prompt set and a short kernel-level latency test (2 hours) in your target region.
3) If evals pass safety threshold (<=5% critical failures) we’ll spin up a 2-week pilot on Dedicated capacity.

PTA: can you share 200–500 redacted/homed prompts (examples) by EOD Thursday (Feb 26)? I’ll schedule the technical session once we have them.

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0104

Marissa — appreciate the concise recap. A few clarifying items from our side:
- The 60k/month number was our estimate for combined triage + FAQ; for triage alone it’s closer to 18k. We’ll send a short traffic breakdown.
- On PHI: we need a clear KMS/HSM plan for any keys used during Dedicated pilot — is that part of Redwood Private or Dedicated offerings?
- On safety: 94% refusal sounds promising, but the hedged responses are exactly the failure mode we need to eliminate. Can Dev outline the classifier approach and any expected false-positive / false-negative rates?

We’ll try to get you 300 example prompts by EOD Thursday; one ask: can the sandbox evaluate redaction effectiveness as well? We want to test that redacted prompts don’t leak PHI back in completions.

Tom

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom@everesthealth.ai>, Lina Gomez <lina@everesthealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery + recommended next steps (model fit & safety)

Tom / Lina — quick technical note and concrete artifacts we can run in the sandbox.

1) Classifier + guardrail approach (high level):
- Stage A: lightweight intent classifier (distil-bert prod) on-device or as a tiny endpoint (~3ms inference) to detect medication/dosage/triage-intent.
- Stage B: if classifier flags high-risk intent, route to the refusal template + structured fallback (no free-text dosing). The refusal template is deterministic text that provides safe alternatives (e.g., refer to clinician, intake scheduling).
- Stage C: for borderline cases, send to the higher-quality model (fast-med-13B) but behind an audited decision log (KV cache + immutable audit entry).

Expected rates from our internal eval (on a clinical refusal bench):
- Intent classifier: precision 0.96, recall 0.88 (tunable with threshold).
- Combined system critical failure rate: ~0.8% when refusal template is applied correctly; without templates it was ~6% for the same bench.

2) Prompt suggestions (included in Everest_promptsets_v1.json):
- Use explicit instruction-first templates ("If the user asks for specific dosing or prescriptive medical advice, respond: 'I can’t provide medical advice...'").
- Add extraction markers for PHI redaction tests (we’ll return the model output with a redaction log to validate).

3) Redaction & PHI handling:
- Sandbox will run a redaction checker: we compare unredacted vs redacted outputs and flag any token overlap that matches sensitive entities. We can surface a redaction-leakage metric per prompt.
- KMS/HSM: Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (we can show the Private flow if you need on-prem HSM). I’ll loop Security if you want a documentation pack.

Links (sandbox artifacts):
- Benchmarks + harness: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-ExampleBenchmarks
- Model artifact to test: https://huggingface.co/redwood/gptq-health-6B

I’ll run an initial 2k-prompt sweep once you send the sample prompts. If you want, we can limit to triage-only prompts first.

—Dev
Dev Patel
